app.title: NeRV – Neuroimaging Results Visualization
app.summary: The person picks an experiment from a page of cards, one card per experiment folder of result files. The experiment opens to a distribution view: one overlaid histogram per dataset-pipeline, with a rug of the individual results and a range slider. Beside it, a summary shows the total number of datapoints and how many results are missing for each pipeline. Clicking a result shows that subject's value, plus each step of the pipeline that produced it, with its status and links to its input, output and task records. In a joint-plot tab, the person picks any two dataset-pipelines as the x and y axes and gets a scatter plot with marginal histograms. Clicking a point shows the result and step-by-step provenance for both pipelines, so they can see whether pipelines agree and trace any odd result back to the processing that made it.

task.text: Check whether different processing pipelines give consistent results for the same measure across subjects, see where results are missing, and trace any single result back to the pipeline steps that produced it.

data.text: One numeric result per subject from each of several processing pipelines, grouped into experiments and dataset files. Each result carries the nested record of the pipeline steps behind it: status, input, output, task and tool-configuration IDs.
data.item: one subject's result from one dataset-pipeline, with the provenance of its processing steps

stage.text: checking the outputs of processing pipelines after they have been run, before trusting the derived measures

mechanism.text: Experiment cards lead to a tabbed page. The distribution tab overlays per-pipeline histograms with a rug and a missing-data summary; the joint-plot tab draws a scatter of any two chosen pipelines, with marginal histograms. In both, clicking a result fills a side panel with that result's pipeline steps in collapsible sections that link to the compute platform's records.

field.text: reproducibility testing of neuroimaging processing pipelines

workflow.name: compare one measure across processing pipelines and trace odd results to their provenance

steps.here: The app is started on a folder of experiment folders. The home page shows one card per experiment, with its last-modified time, and choosing a card loads every JSON results file in that folder into one table.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Per-pipeline histograms of the result are overlaid, coloured by dataset-pipeline, with a rug of the individual values. A range slider narrows the axis.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: A summary card counts the total datapoints, the missing results, and the missing results for each dataset-pipeline.

Clicking a result in the histogram shows its subject, pipeline and value, then each pipeline step in a collapsible section. Each section gives the step's status and links to its input, output and task records.
x and y dropdowns choose any two dataset-pipelines. Their results are drawn against each other in a scatter plot with marginal histograms and a range slider.
Clicking a scatter point lists the subject, result and step-by-step provenance for the x pipeline and then for the y pipeline.

distinctive: Missing results are kept out of the histogram but counted for each pipeline, so pipeline failures show as plainly as the values do.
Every result keeps the chain of processing steps that made it, with each step's status and links to its input, output and task records on the compute platform.
Each data file gets its own sequential colour scale, and the pipelines within a file are shades of it, which caps how many pipelines and files can be shown.
The comparison is between pipelines that compute the same measure, not between conditions or samples.
